title: [Runner] Fix false-positive Win+Shift+C shortcut conflict on Windows 11

status.label: Review in progress
status.detail: The corrected generated scenario passes Windows PowerShell 5.1 parsing and AST checks with a real catch/finally boundary, rather than a standalone uninvoked script block. This is static evidence only. The fixture intentionally uses a private mock lock and cannot by itself prove release of the actual shared validation lock. A separate wrapper was prepared, but its assigned runtime attempt stopped before execution because a wait failure in its cleanup path could bypass lock disposal without confirmed child exit. No lock, child, fixture runtime or product command was started in that attempt. The wrapper is under source-only repair. Product validation also remains independently gated on the configured dependency cache's exact provenance; a different cache must not be substituted or its hash adopted without justification.

next_action: Resume the saved review stage in the next dashboard update.
